lists.content:
As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you own the whole job for a customer: understand the problem, design the solution, build it with Claude Code and other AI coding tools, roll it out, and keep it running.
This is a hands-on role that sits close to the customer. You will talk to them, understand how their business works, and turn that into software they use every day. You own what you build, from the first line of code to live in production.
You will not be one small cog in a large system. You will ship whole things.

This role is for you if - 
  • You have worked as a solutions engineer, implementation engineer, or in a similar delivery role, and you now want to build the product, not just configure it
  • You like being in front of customers and owning delivery end-to-end
  • You want to ship with the newest AI coding tools and grow fast

• Run discovery with customers to understand how their business works and what they need
  • Design the solution, then build it using Claude Code or similar AI harnesses
  • Take a customer problem and turn it into a working product, end to end
  • Roll out and onboard the product with the customer, and train their team to use it
  • Deploy and maintain what you build on our stack
  • Fix bugs, add features, and keep customer products running and reliable
  • Work with customers and internal teams to scope what to build next
  • Answer customer queries about how their product works and how their data is handled

• 1 to 2 years of experience building or delivering software for customers. This can be as a software engineer, solutions engineer, implementation engineer, or similar.
  • You have built and deployed at least one full web app, at work or as a personal project
  • You are comfortable with modern application frameworks
  • You already use AI coding tools like Claude Code, Cursor, or similar, and you are good at it
  • You can work with a database and deploy to the cloud
  • You are good with customers. You can run a call, ask the right questions, and explain things simply.
  • You are based in Bengaluru and can work onsite
  • You are comfortable with working hours that overlap with US customers

• You'll be part of an early team at a fast-growing company, with a lot of impact
  • You'll get to work with really smart and helpful people
  • We constantly adopt the latest technologies and stay close to the latest ai innovations
  • Opportunity to influence the direction of the product and engineering culture
  • Flexible PTO policy
  • Unlimited ai usage
  • Plus cool swag, a stocked pantry, and other benefits

lists.content:
Gushwork's content programmes run on our customers' own websites, on their domain, alongside everything else already there. Making that work means dealing with whatever infrastructure a business has accumulated over a decade: DNS configured by an agency that is no longer involved, a CDN nobody set up deliberately, redirect rules that predate the current marketing team. Every customer is a different version of that problem.

The Implementation Engineer owns it. The role sits closer to engineering, and combines hands-on technical setup with direct customer communication.

• Own the technical implementation for new customers end to end: review their environment, access, configuration and technical dependencies ahead of implementation, take the setup live, and verify the result.

  • Work directly with customers to configure and validate setups, including calls with their in-house developers or agency partners as well as their marketing teams.

  • Diagnose customer-specific issues across websites, APIs, networking and web infrastructure, and determine what can be resolved independently and what requires Engineering.

  • Own the customer-facing communication end to end. Validate the fix, then explain what happened in language a non-technical stakeholder can act on.

  • Establish where a customer's domain, DNS and hosting access sits, including on older setups where this is not documented, and confirm the results of automated checks before relying on them.

  • Reduce recurring issues through documentation, improvements to the implementation process, and structured feedback to Product and Engineering.

  • Partner with Customer Success, Engineering and Web Development to gather context on customer requirements and share technical findings.

This role requires two things together. Most candidates have one.

  • Strong technical depth. Working knowledge of HTTP/HTTPS, DNS, domains, reverse proxies, CDNs, caching, SSL and basic networking, at a level sufficient to debug them rather than describe them.

  • Strong written and verbal communication. In particular, the ability to explain a technical issue in simple language to somebody who is frustrated. This is roughly half the role.

  • Willingness to work in US hours (6pm to 3am) — our customers are primarily based in the US, so the role requires flexibility to work in US time zones.

    • In addition:

  • 2 to 5 years of experience. Candidates earlier in their career who have hands-on experience operating web infrastructure, including on their own projects, are welcome to make the case in their application.

  • The ability to reason about two systems at once. Most answers here depend on how a customer's setup and our product interact, rather than on either in isolation.

  • Strong investigative ability. Reading logs, configurations and documentation to form and test a hypothesis about an unfamiliar problem.

  • The ability to make progress independently on an unfamiliar technical issue, rather than routing it onward as a first step.

  • Ownership and follow-through, including holding several open issues at once without losing the urgent one.

• Experience with reverse proxies, Cloudflare, DNS, CDNs, web servers, APIs or webhooks.

  • Documentation or help content you have written that measurably reduced a category of customer questions.

lists.content:
• Drive Cross-Functional Performance:Act as the "Product CEO" for your domain; proactively hunting for friction in the user journey and engineering the connective tissue between Product, Sales, and Success.
  • Architect Agentic Systems: Design and deploy autonomous AI workflows (n8n, APIs, LLMs) that move beyond linear logic to automate reasoning-based tasks across Sales and Support.
  • Ship High-Fidelity Prototypes: Rapidly build and own internal tools or "makeshift" features using no-code stacks (Retool, Lovable) to unblock GTM teams and validate ideas before Engineering commits code.
  • Operationalize Product Intelligence: Bridge the gap between raw data and strategy by using SQL and LLMs to synthesize unstructured feedback into high-signal roadmap priorities.
  • Command Full-Cycle Rollouts: Own the "last mile"—from technical QA and automated migrations to the enablement of CS and Sales—ensuring every feature is commercially and operationally ready.

Must-Have
  • 2+ years of experience in Product Management, Product Ops, or Growth at a fast-growing B2B SaaS company.
  • Basic AI Native Literacy: Beyond "chatting" with AI. Proven ability to design structured, version-controlled prompts (XML/Markdown tagging) for production use in internal tools or customer-facing features.
  • Strategic Analytical Skills: Advanced proficiency in SQL and data visualization (Tableau, Looker, or PostHog). You should be comfortable performing cohort analysis and funnel modeling independently.
  • Automation Expertise: Deep experience with Claude Code, n8n, including handling webhooks, API authentication, and error mapping.
  • Full-Cycle Ownership: Experience taking a product or major feature from initial concept through to post-launch optimization.
  • The "Startup Mindset": You thrive in ambiguity and are a "builder" by nature. You’d rather ship an 80% solution today than a 100% solution in three months.
  • Technical Background: Ability to read/write basic JavaScript or Python for API debugging and custom logic within no-code tools.
    •  
    Good to have
  • Non-Deterministic QA: In an LLM world, features don't just "work" or "break"—they hallucinate. You must have experience building using LLM tech stack.
  • Eval frameworks (using tools like Braintrust, LangSmith, or custom spreadsheets) to measure the accuracy, tone, and reliability of AI-generated outputs.
  • Cost & Latency Management: Ability to make trade-offs between model power (e.g., GPT-4o) and efficiency (e.g., GPT-4o-mini/Claude Haiku) based on the business value of the use case.
  • Agentic Frameworks: Hands-on experience or deep familiarity with orchestrating LLM agents (e.g., using LangChain, CrewAI, or n8n’s AI nodes) to perform multi-step, non-linear tasks.

• Competitive base salary + performance-based bonus.
  • Meaningful equity — you’ll be an early partner in our growth.
  • Work directly with both the founders. No layers at all at this point.
  • Access to all the tools, software, and resources (analytics, content, experiments, design, etc.)Budget for professional development — courses, books, conferences.
  • Group Insurance Coverages for Health, Personal Accident, Term Life & OPD Benefits; flexible time off.
  • A fast-moving, high-autonomy environment where your voice is heard.

lists.content:
• help build and ship next-generation features on our platform - ai-led content research, web page generation and ai-led content updates

  • manage ui applications and infrastructure for backend services across ecs, step functions, lambdas, etc.

  • keep systems performant, robust, and reliable through last-mile performance tuning, observability, and monitoring

  • collaborate with product and design teams to understand problems and propose technical solutions

  • write clear docs and runbooks for systems and processes

fullstack ownership

  • you have shipped production features that span a modern web UI and backend APIs, not only one layer

  • you are comfortable owning a bet from ticket to production - scoping, implementation, monitoring, and iteration

  • you can hold UI, API contracts, data model, and deployment in mind at once without losing the customer outcome

    • product minded

  • you tie technical work to customer and roadmap impact - you ask when and why is unclear instead of guessing

  • you prefer small, reviewable PRs and measurable rollout over large surprise diffs

    • ai native

  • you have built or operated software where LLMs or AI pipelines are part of the product path - code generation, orchestration, evals, cost, testability and reliability included

  • you care about quality, cost, and failure modes of AI-assisted flows (latency, retries, evals, human-in-the-loop where needed)

    • fullstack capabilities

  • you have worked on Node.js and/or Python, Next and/or React in production at meaningful traffic or data volume

  • you are comfortable working on frontend, backend, and infrastructure across the stack, without reservations

  • you know how to maintain reliable systems while shipping fast - observability (e.g. Sentry), sane defaults, and pragmatic tradeoffs

  • you know how to build and ship ci/cd pipelines

    • craft

  • you treat and nurture your code like a piece of art, with the right balance of simplicity and complexity, without sacrificing speed

  • you have a high bias to action (run those POCs with cursor/claude code), and a low bias to over-engineering

    • human

  • you build trust with PMs, designers, and engineers - async updates in Slack, threads not @channel noise

  • you admit what you do not know and pull in the right owner (buddy, infra, security) early

  • you explain complex ideas clearly in writing - specs, PR descriptions, and docs

  • you hold 3+ years of experience

• you'll be part of an early team at a fast-growing company, with a lot of impact

  • you'll get to work with really smart and helpful people

  • we constantly adopt the latest technologies and stay close to the latest ai innovations

  • opportunity to influence the direction of the product and engineering culture

  • flexible PTO policy

  • unlimited ai usage

  • plus cool swag, a stocked pantry, and other benefits
